newsitem.title: TURKEY: Fire extinguished at Turkish oil tanker.
newsitem.headline: Fire extinguished at Turkish oil tanker.

text.p: Firefighters on Friday extinguished a blaze at a docked Turkish oil tanker that had injured 18 people, Anatolian news agency said.
Istanbul fire brigade helped by experts from a refinery in the coastal city of Izmir doused the flames at the TPAO tanker in the early hours of the morning, it said.
The TPAO, at 159,982 deadweight tonnes, is Turkey's biggest oil tanker. The vessel, built in 1977 and owned by Turkish company Ditas, was in the yard at Istanbul for repairs and carried no oil.
Most of those injured in the blaze were firemen. A local official said the fire started on Thursday after an explosion in the gas depot.
